Incident Workflow

Incident runbook

A blameless, step-by-step process for detecting, triaging, escalating, resolving, and learning from API incidents caught by SignalForge.

Under active incident?

Skip to Phase 2: Triage immediately. First responder: acknowledge the alert before reading any further.

Incident lifecycle overview

SignalForge organizes incident response into five phases. Each phase has a clear owner, timebox, and exit criteria. The phases are sequential but may overlap during fast-moving incidents.

#PhaseOwnerTimeboxExit criteria
1 Detect Automated (SignalForge) < 2 min Alert delivered to on-call channel
2 Triage First responder < 5 min Severity confirmed, IC assigned
3 Escalate Incident commander < 10 min Stakeholders notified, war room open
4 Resolve Incident commander Variable Service restored, signal resolved
5 Post-mortem Team < 48 hr Post-mortem doc published, action items filed

Phase 1 — Detect

1
Detection (automated)
T+0:00 → T+2:00

SignalForge handles detection automatically. When a monitor check fails, the engine evaluates your alert rules and dispatches signals to configured destinations. A typical critical signal looks like this:

Slack alert — #platform-alerts text 
[CRITICAL] payments-api-health → status_not_2xx

Monitor:   Payments API Health
Value:     HTTP 503
Threshold: 2xx
Failures:  2 consecutive (after_failures: 2)
Regions:   us-east-1, eu-west-1
Started:   2024-03-12T14:32:18Z
Signal ID: sig_01HXK9F2J8

→ View in dashboard: app.signalforge.io/signals/sig_01HXK9F2J8
→ Acknowledge: signalforge ack sig_01HXK9F2J8

What happens automatically:

  • Monitor probe fails from configured regions
  • Consecutive-failure threshold crossed (configurable via after_failures)
  • Alert rule evaluated — severity determined
  • Signal dispatched to all matching destinations (Slack, PagerDuty, webhook)
  • Deduplication applied — you get one alert per signal, not one per check

Phase 2 — Triage

2
Triage
T+0:00 → T+5:00

The first responder (on-call engineer) triages within 5 minutes of the alert. Goal: understand what's broken, how bad it is, and whether to escalate.

Triage checklist

  • Acknowledge the alert: signalforge ack <signal_id> or click Acknowledge in the dashboard
  • Confirm signal is real (not a probe flap) — check consecutive_failures count and region spread
  • Pull recent signal history: signalforge signals --monitor payments-api-health --limit 20
  • Check correlated monitors — is it isolated or are multiple services affected?
  • Classify severity: critical (customer impact now) vs. warning (degraded, not broken)
  • Post triage status to #platform-incidents Slack channel
Triage commands bash 
# Acknowledge a signal
$ signalforge ack sig_01HXK9F2J8
✓ Signal sig_01HXK9F2J8 acknowledged

# Get recent signal history for a monitor
$ signalforge signals --monitor payments-api-health --limit 10

TIME (UTC)           TYPE                  SEVERITY  VALUE      DURATION
──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
2024-03-12 14:32:18  status_not_2xx        CRITICAL  HTTP 503   ongoing
2024-03-12 09:14:03  latency_p95_exceeded  WARNING   2,342ms    8m 12s
2024-03-11 22:01:55  status_not_2xx        CRITICAL  HTTP 502   2m 44s

# Check all active signals across workspace
$ signalforge signals --state firing

sig_01HXK9F2J8  payments-api-health  status_not_2xx  CRITICAL  2m ago
Single-region vs multi-region failures

A failure in only one region often indicates a network or DNS issue rather than an application problem. A failure in all regions almost always means the service itself is down. Check the regions array in the signal payload before assuming full outage.

Phase 3 — Escalate

3
Escalation
T+5:00 → T+15:00

Escalation criteria depend on severity and time-to-acknowledge. SignalForge auto-escalates via your alert rule configuration if the signal is unacknowledged after a configurable timeout (default: 10 minutes for critical).

Manual escalation path

SeverityImmediate actionAuto-escalate afterEscalation target
critical Page on-call via PagerDuty 10 min unacknowledged Engineering manager
warning Post to #platform-alerts 30 min unresolved On-call engineer
info Record in signal history Never (no escalation) —

War room checklist (critical only)

  • Assign Incident Commander (IC) — typically the most senior engineer on-call
  • Open Zoom/Slack huddle in #incident-live channel
  • IC posts initial incident summary: time of detection, affected service, customer impact estimate
  • Notify Customer Success if customer-facing impact is confirmed
  • Begin timeline doc — log every action with UTC timestamp
  • Add maintenance window if needed: signalforge maintenance create --monitor payments-api-health --duration 60m
Example escalation rule in signalforge.yml yaml 
rules:
  - id: payments-critical-escalation
    when:
      signal_type: status_not_2xx
      monitor_id: payments-api-health
      severity: critical
    notify:
      - channel: pagerduty-oncall
        immediately: true
      - channel: pagerduty-manager
        after_unacked_minutes: 10
      - channel: slack-platform
        immediately: true

Phase 4 — Resolve

4
Resolution
Variable

Resolution happens when the underlying issue is fixed and SignalForge detects that the monitor is healthy again. The engine emits a *_recovered signal and notifies the same destinations as the original alert.

Resolution checklist

  • Confirm fix is deployed or rollback is complete
  • Wait for SignalForge to auto-detect recovery (usually within one monitor interval)
  • Or manually verify: signalforge status --monitor payments-api-health
  • Confirm status_recovered signal appears in signal history
  • Post all-clear message to #platform-incidents with: time resolved, duration, brief impact summary
  • Close PagerDuty incident if applicable
  • Remove maintenance window if one was created: signalforge maintenance end --monitor payments-api-health
Confirming recovery bash 
$ signalforge signals --monitor payments-api-health --limit 5

TIME (UTC)           TYPE                SEVERITY  VALUE    DURATION
─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
2024-03-12 14:36:50  status_recovered    INFO      HTTP 200  —
2024-03-12 14:32:18  status_not_2xx      CRITICAL  HTTP 503  4m 32s

$ signalforge status --monitor payments-api-health

payments-api-health   ● OK   14s ago   downtime today: 4m 32s

Phase 5 — Post-mortem

5
Blameless Post-mortem
Within 48 hours

For any critical incident, file a blameless post-mortem within 48 hours. SignalForge automatically generates a signal timeline to anchor the document.

Generate timeline for post-mortem bash 
$ signalforge postmortem --signal sig_01HXK9F2J8 --format markdown

# Post-mortem: payments-api-health — 2024-03-12

## Timeline
- 14:32:18Z  SignalForge detected HTTP 503 (region: us-east-1)
- 14:32:48Z  SignalForge confirmed HTTP 503 (region: eu-west-1)
- 14:32:49Z  Critical alert dispatched (Slack + PagerDuty)
- 14:33:22Z  Signal acknowledged by @jamie
- 14:35:00Z  Rollback initiated (deploy d4b8a92)
- 14:36:50Z  HTTP 200 restored — signal resolved
- Total downtime: 4m 32s

Post-mortem document template

  • Summary — 2–3 sentence description of what happened and its impact
  • Timeline — generated via signalforge postmortem --signal <id>
  • Root cause — what actually caused the failure (code, config, infrastructure, external dep)
  • Detection quality — did SignalForge catch it before a customer? How quickly?
  • What went well — response time, communication, tooling
  • What could improve — gaps in coverage, slow response, missing runbook steps
  • Action items — specific, owned, time-boxed tasks to prevent recurrence
Blameless means finding the system failure

A good post-mortem asks "what in our system allowed this to happen?" not "who made the mistake?" People operate in the systems we build. Fix the system.

Signal reference for on-call

Quick reference for interpreting the most common production signals:

Signal typeMeaningFirst thing to check
status_not_2xx HTTP endpoint returned non-2xx status Error logs, recent deploys, upstream dependencies
latency_p95_exceeded 95th percentile response time above threshold Database slow queries, N+1 queries, cold cache
tcp_timeout TCP connection timed out — port unreachable Security group / firewall rules, network path
cert_expiry_critical TLS certificate expires in < 7 days Certificate renewal process, auto-renew configuration
body_mismatch Response body didn't match expected content Maintenance page served, wrong environment, routing error
dns_resolution_failed DNS lookup failed for monitored hostname DNS propagation, zone file changes, registrar issues
